_comment: FLEET PREFERENCES — selectively enable/disable priorities and behaviours. The SHAPE (committed).
Live copy is substrate/preferences.json (gitignored: it is this fleet's operating choices, not a fact
about the game). Every strategy switch this repo grows should land here as a named toggle rather than
as a hardcoded constant, so it can be turned on or off without a code change or a restart of judgement.
THE CONTRACT (same as the other local files, docs/m59-policy.md): a missing file or a missing key means
the committed default, never 'off'. An unrecognised key is reported, never silently dropped. `enabled:
false` disables a preference; removing it reverts to the default. Tools read this; where a preference
must reach a keeper (a movement ban), the order scripts resolve it into per-character policy and push it.
Each entry is { enabled, ...params }. Add new ones freely — the reader ignores shapes it does not know

avoid_locations.why: Places the fleet must not route into — a movement ban, resolved into each character's banned_destinations.

rules.reason: Roq's tunnel (A shadowy corner) — rats and lupoggs block pathing; sellers die there. Temporary while the tunnel is unsafe.
EXAMPLE: a PVP flashpoint — flip enabled:true to keep the fleet out of a town while flagged players are active there.
EXAMPLE: avoid a whole map. Toggle per event.

sell_circuit.why: The Barloque multi-stop sell run (equipment->smith, gems->jeweler, reagents->herbalist). Disable to fall back to the single-shop sell (Roq) — which is currently also banned, so disabling both means carry-and-hold.

advancement_split.why: Route by max HP: below the threshold to prey that still advances you, at/over it to tougher prey. Disable to leave characters wherever they are.

roam.why: Let characters move between rooms for their prey rather than being pinned. Disable to re-pin with assigned_room.
